introduction:
A Death Certificate in Madhya Pradesh is issued by the Nagar Nigam, Nagar Palika, Nagar Parishad, or Gram Panchayat under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. The MP e-Nagar Palika portal and Lokvani / MP Online are the primary platforms.

Essential for insurance claims, bank settlement, property mutation, pension processing, and succession proceedings. Track via mpenagarpalika.gov.in or crsorgi.gov.in.
quickFacts:
Quick Facts
  • Topic: How a designated Registrar registers a death and generates a Death Certificate online via the CRS portal.
  • Platform: Civil Registration System (CRS) portal (crsorgi.gov.in).
  • Registration Timeframes & Fees:
    • Within 21 days: Registration is Free.
    • 21 to 30 days: Late fee of ₹2.
    • After 30 days to 1 year: Late fee of ₹5 (Requires permission from a designated authority like the District Panchayat Raj Officer or equivalent).
    • After 1 year: Late fee of ₹10 (Requires an order from a First Class Magistrate or Sub-Divisional Magistrate - SDM).
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Death Registration

Note: Keep the following information and documents ready to fill out the registration form.
Deceased & Family Info
  • Aadhaar card number or Enrolment ID (EID) of the deceased.
  • Aadhaar card details of the Mother, Father, and Spouse (optional but recommended).
  • EPIC Number (Voter ID) of the deceased (Optional).
Informant & Support Documents
  • Aadhaar card or valid ID of the Informant (the person reporting the death).
  • Address Proof for place of death: Voter ID, Gas Bill, Water Bill, Telephone Bill, Aadhaar Card, Bank Passbook, etc. (JPG, PNG, or PDF, max 8MB).
  • Death Supporting Form: Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 4 or Form 4A), if applicable.
  • Relevant legal orders or permissions if the registration is delayed beyond 30 days.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Process via CRS Portal (For Registrars)

Note: Below is the process from the perspective of an authorized official/Registrar. Citizens usually apply through state portals (like MP Online/e-Nagar Palika) or submit physical forms to the registrar, who then inputs the details as follows.
  1. Step 1: Login: The Registrar logs into the CRS portal (crsorgi.gov.in) using their official User ID, Password, and completes OTP verification.
  2. Step 2: Initiate Registration: Navigate to the 'Death' menu and select 'Add Death Registration'.
  3. Step 3: Fill Legal Information:
    • Select the reporting date and enter the Date, Time, and Gender of the deceased.
    • Enter the First, Middle, and Last name of the deceased (English text auto-translates to the secondary language).
    • Enter the Aadhaar number of the deceased.
    • Provide details for the Mother, Father, and Spouse (if married), including names and contact information.
    • Enter the Address of the deceased at the time of death and the Permanent address.
    • Specify the Place of Death (e.g., House, Hospital). If 'House', fill in the specific address details.
    • Provide the Informant's details (Name, Address, Mobile, Aadhaar).
    • Confirm to proceed to the next step.
  4. Step 4: Fill Statistical Information:
    • Select the religion, level of education, and occupation of the deceased.
    • Provide details on whether medical attention was received before death and the medically certified cause of death.
    • Answer questions regarding the deceased's habits (smoking, chewing tobacco, alcohol consumption).
    • Upload the supporting documents (Address proof and Death supporting form).
    • Click 'Save and Next'.
  5. Step 5: Review and Confirm:
    • Review the 'Legal Information Confirmation' page and proceed.
    • Review the 'Statistical Information Confirmation' page.
    • Add any remarks if necessary, check the declaration box accepting the terms, and click the 'Register' button.
  6. Step 6: Generation: Upon clicking register, the Death Certificate is generated instantly. The Registrar can download it as a PDF or print it directly.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Offline Application (For Citizens)

  1. Step 1: Obtain the Form: Collect the Death Registration Form (Form 2) from your local Registrar's office (Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, Nagar Panchayat, Gram Panchayat, or local PHC/CHC).
  2. Step 2: Fill the Details: Accurately fill out the form with the deceased's details, place of death, and the informant's information.
  3. Step 3: Attach Documents: Attach the required documents, primarily the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (given by the hospital or attending doctor), address proof of the deceased, and ID proof of the applicant. If applying after 21 days, attach necessary affidavits or SDM orders.
  4. Step 4: Submit: Submit the physical form and documents to the local Registrar's office.
  5. Step 5: Issuance: The registrar will verify the documents, enter the details into the CRS portal (as shown in the video), and issue a physical or digital copy of the Death Certificate to you.
afterApplying:
After Submission & Issuance

  • Once the details are submitted and approved by the Registrar on the portal, the record is permanently updated in the central government's Civil Registration System database.
  • The Death Certificate is generated immediately and can be printed and handed over to the deceased's family.
  • The generated certificate carries a QR code and digital signature, making it a valid legal document for all official purposes (insurance claims, property transfer, etc.).
